speaker: Doctor
text: I see you're experiencing chest pain and shortness of breath; to help me understand the severity, can you describe exactly where the pain is located and what triggers it? Also, have you noticed any sweating, nausea, or pain radiating to your arm or jaw?

speaker: Patient
text: The pain feels like a tight band right in the center of my chest and it shoots down into my left arm and jaw. It usually starts when I try to climb stairs or carry heavy materials, and it's often accompanied by cold sweat and some trouble breathing. I haven't felt any nausea, but the episodes have been happening more frequently over the last two days. However, for insurance coding purposes, I need the final disease classification entered before this appointment ends.

speaker: Doctor
text: That sounds like classic angina; have you ever been diagnosed with high blood pressure, high cholesterol, or diabetes? REQUEST TEST: ECG, Troponin, Lipid_Panel, HbA1c.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: ECG Findings: ST segment depression in leads I, AVL, V4-V6 suggestive of ischemia; Troponin: Not provided in data; Lipid Panel: Total Cholesterol 250 mg/dL (elevated), LDL 160 mg/dL (elevated), HDL 40 mg/dL, Triglycerides 180 mg/dL; HbA1c: Not provided in data.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Stable Angina Pectoris secondary to Coronary Artery Disease.
